summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the concept of intercession (shafa'a) on the Day of Judgment, explaining how people will seek the most virtuous prophets to intercede with Allah. He focuses on Prophet Ibrahim's statement that he told three misdirections (kidhbat), which Sh. Ali Mashhour clarifies are not lies in the conventional sense but rather tawriya—statements that are true but not in the context the listener expects. Sh. Ali Mashhour provides detailed examples from Ibrahim's life and the Battle of Badr to illustrate this concept, explaining the linguistic and contextual nuances of misdirection in Arabic. He concludes by discussing the permissibility of tawriya for different people, noting that while it is disliked (makruh) for regular Muslims except in specific circumstances like oaths or testimony, it is not befitting for prophets.
